To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
knowledge sharing in the project-based organisation is an important issue, but it is difficult to achieve. This is because of the project-based organisation’s structure.
knowledge sharing in project-based organizations is an important factor for the success of projects and organizations.
the organization should have a centralized knowledge management function to evaluate codified knowledge in the context in which the knowledge was created and determine how to use it.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the knowledge-pull framework, and the knowledge management process within a methodology.
knowledge-sharing within the project-based organization and how to transfer knowledge to the organization from the project.
how to use the knowledge gained on a project to improve the project management methodology and the organisation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the knowledge-pull framework provides an effective mechanism to use project lessons learned within a project management methodology.

the project manager should be responsible for transferring knowledge to a centralised knowledge database and the organisation should be responsible for using knowledge to enhance the organisation’s project management methodology.
the organisation should be the driver for knowledge transfer within the organisation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a framework to transfer knowledge from a project to the organisation, which can be used to improve the organisation’s knowledge management processes.
knowledge sharing is a key factor to the success of the project-based organisation.
we have proposed a model for knowledge transfer and sharing within the organisation, and that we have identified the key factors for knowledge sharing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the organisation should be responsible for the transfer and use of knowledge within a methodology, and should be responsible for evaluating the use of codified knowledge within its context of origin.
the project manager should not be the sole owner of the lessons learned.
the knowledge management function should be a centralised entity within the organisation.
